messages.subject: problem with transformed parameter block
parts:
I'm trying to fit a fairly simple multilevel logistic regression model (attached) to data from a perception experiment using PyStan. The model consists of listener, stimulus-category, stimulus-talker, and various parent parameters. I tried to include the following transformed parameters block to calculate the predicted probability (this block is in the attached file, commented out). The arrays sb, st, and tk contain indices for the listener, stimulus category, and stimulus talker, respectively.

transformed parameters {
    row_vector<lower=0,upper=1>[ntr] theta[nsb]; // predicted probability
    for(sbi in 1:nsb)
        for(tri in 1:ntr)
            theta[sbi,tri] = inv_logit(beta[sb[sbi]] + alpha[st[sbi,tri],tk[sbi,tri]]);
}

However, I got the following error. I tried it with theta defined as real<lower=0,upper=1> theta[nsb,ntr] and got the same error. I also tried it with curly brackets enclosing the nested loops, but that didn't help.

ValueError: Error parsing model code:
SYNTAX ERROR, MESSAGE(S) FROM PARSER:
Illegal statement beginning with non-void expression parsed as
  get_base1(get_base1(theta,sbi,"theta",1),tri,"theta",2)
Not a legal assignment, sampling, or function statement.  Note that
  * Assignment statements only allow variables (with optional indexes) on the left;
    if you see an outer function logical_lt (<) with negated (-) second argument,
    it indicates an assignment statement A <- B with illegal left
    side A parsed as expression (A < (-B)).
  * Sampling statements allow arbitrary value-denoting expressions on the left.
  * Functions used as statements must be declared to have void returns


ERROR at line 23
 21:        for(sbi in 1:nsb)
 22:            for(tri in 1:ntr)
 23:                theta[sbi,tri] = inv_logit(beta[sb[sbi]] + alpha[st[sbi,tri],tk[sbi,tri]]);
                    ^
 24:    }

The attached model works, with the inv_logit() term used as an argument to the bernoulli() distribution function (i.e., it compiles and I can get samples of the posterior distribution). I was able to get a similar model working using a transformed parameters block much like this using RStan a while back. Any ideas about why this is causing problems here would be appreciated, as would thoughts and suggestions about the pros and cons of constructing this kind of model with or without the transformed parameters block.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] problem with transformed parameter block
parts:
The syntax is "<-" for assignment in Stan. I should
add an error message that recognizes "=" in the same
contexts and raises an appropriate error message.

- Bob
